message.content:
The total number of distinct positions that can arise in a standard game of chess is astronomically large – on the order of **10⁴³**.  

This figure comes from Shannon’s estimate of the “Shannon number” (≈10⁴³) for the size of the game tree, which counts all legal positions reachable from the starting position. More recent computational studies suggest the number of legal positions is somewhere between 10⁴² and 10⁴⁴, but it is still roughly 10⁴³. If you include illegal positions (e.g., those that violate the rules), the count rises to about 10⁴⁷.
